children: The accelerating AI buildout and heavy government borrowing were intensifying competition for capital, with U.S. financing demand potentially exceeding $7.5T annually by 2030, according to a BlackRock note

The note said the financing needs of the AI buildout were adding to already elevated government borrowing, creating what it described as the most intense competition for capital since the global financial crisis and the COVID-19 shock.
AI and data-center bonds accounted for about 14% of U.S. investment-grade issuance in 2026, up from 5% in 2025 and 1% over the previous decade, the institute said.
The institute said the financing wave still had room to run despite concerns about slower development of frontier AI models.
Most AI compute was being used for inference, or running existing models, rather than training new ones, suggesting demand for compute could remain strong even if progress on frontier models slowed.

Higher borrowing costs were also being reinforced by energy prices. The Strait of Hormuz remained effectively closed amid the Middle East conflict, while Brent crude had moved back above $100 a barrel, adding to sticky inflation pressures.
BlackRock said a spillover from higher energy prices into wages and other costs could make core inflation more persistent and keep monetary policy tighter for longer.
U.S. Treasury yields had risen the previous week following the Federal Reserve's rate hike, with the 10-year Treasury yield

BlackRock said markets risked overinterpreting the hawkish tone of Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's post-meeting comments while arguing that a rate hike that reinforced Fed credibility amid strong growth could coexist with a pro-risk market stance.

BlackRock maintained an overweight view on U.S. equities and AI, citing resilient corporate earnings, while favoring short- and medium-term government bonds over longer-duration debt. It also favored credit with attractive coupons while avoiding the weakest borrowers and companies issuing large amounts of debt.

The institute said it would watch upcoming flash PMIs for signs that business activity in the U.S., UK, and Europe was holding up as borrowing costs rose. Further U.S. resilience, it said, would reinforce the case for rates staying higher for longer.

title: BlackRock sees AI buildout intensifying competition for capital
